claims.claim_vi: The source names six server types: web, mail, DNS, proxy, FTP and origin server. Only the names are reused; the lesson explains each type in its own words.
claims.section: Top 6 most commonly used server types
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: MDN: a server is software or hardware offering a service to a client; a web server is software that often runs on a hardware server; a web server sends an HTML file to the browser.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: a CDN is a group of servers spread over many locations that store duplicate copies of data so that the servers closest to the end users can fulfil requests.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: a proxy server is an intermediate program or computer that intercepts requests and serves back responses; it may forward the requests or not (for example a cache) and may modify them (for example headers); the two main types are a forward proxy and a reverse proxy.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: DNS is a hierarchical and decentralized naming system; its most prominent function is translating a human-friendly domain name into a numeric IP address, and a reverse lookup finds the domain name for an address.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: SMTP is a protocol used to send a new email; IMAP is a protocol used to retrieve and store emails and allows folders and rules on the server.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: FTP is an insecure protocol for transferring files from one host to another; it was the de facto standard way but many hosting accounts no longer support it, and a secure, encrypted method should be used instead.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: RFC 9110: the term origin server refers to a program that can originate authoritative responses for a given target resource; a gateway (reverse proxy) is an intermediary that acts as an origin server for the outbound connection; a proxy is a message-forwarding agent chosen by the client.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: An origin server may build a response at request time from application logic and data (a dynamic or personalised resource), so it does not necessarily hold a master copy; a CDN holds copies that can answer in its place (MDN, CDN page).
claims.verified_by: RFC 9110 defines the role by authoritative responses (read); the dynamic-resource example is the author's general knowledge.

claims.claim_vi: An IP address is a network-layer address assigned to a network interface of a device; it is not necessarily a single decimal-number sequence and does not necessarily identify exactly one machine. The grouping of the six types into two sets, the statement that the six types are roles rather than machines, and the typical order of events for a page load are the author's general knowledge.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against primary documentation.

claims.claim_vi: A browser that already holds a usable cached DNS answer does not query a DNS server for the page load, and behind a forward proxy the proxy may resolve the host name; the DNS-first answer therefore describes the cache-miss, direct-resolution path.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against primary documentation.

design_notes_vi: Sáu thẻ chia hai nhóm: ba loại đưa nội dung tới người dùng và ba loại dịch vụ nền của mạng. Không có mũi tên vì nguồn không nói thứ tự giữa các loại. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source lists six server types in one flat order (web, mail, DNS, proxy, FTP, origin) with one sentence each; the lesson keeps only the six names, regroups them into two sets by position on the path of a request and writes its own explanation of each (MDN glossary pages for web server, proxy, CDN, DNS, SMTP, IMAP and FTP; RFC 9110 for the origin server) instead of translating the source sentences.
The lesson qualifies the DNS-first answer as the cache-miss, direct-resolution path (author's general knowledge).
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Phần giải thích dựa vào các trang từ điển thuật ngữ của MDN và kiến thức chung của người biên soạn, chưa đối chiếu với tài liệu chuẩn. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
